hook: "this mini VSL style ad is the highest converting format we've tested — especially for telehealth"
body: The method: highest-converting mini-VSL style for telehealth = authority figure direct to camera, feels like advice not an ad, made with OMNI flash + GPT Image 2. The craft rules: match the avatar to who trusts the offer (older, credible, not a model); lock the character once, generate all frames in GPT Image 2; animate in Omni Flash with the same lock in every prompt; keep gestures small, no big movements. 43s video.

sequencing: Hook: highest-converting mini-VSL, telehealth.
The format: authority figure as advice, built with OMNI Flash + GPT Image 2.
The caveat: script + avatar must land or it falls flat.
Rule 1: match avatar to who trusts the offer.
Rule 2: lock the character, generate all frames.
Rule 3: same lock in every animation prompt.
Rule 4: small gestures only.
43s video.

hook: "This Eskiin ad is by far one of the best founder-led DTC ads I've seen lately. And it's not because the founders are charismatic. It's because the ad barely feels like an ad for the first half."
body: The Eskiin ad structure, decoded: opens with a vision board — a 16-year-old kid, one goal: retire his mom (open loop: how did he do it?). Then PERSONAL STORY → PROBLEM (eczema, dry skin, hair loss, rashes) → FAILED SOLUTIONS (medications, shampoos, treatments) → DISCOVERY/reframe ('Could it be our water?') → MECHANISM → PRODUCT (filtered showerhead built around everything hated in alternatives: Amazon = cheap junk, existing = weak pressure, expensive = still not good enough) → MISSION zoom-out ('building the company we wish existed': American fulfillment, no dropshipping, customer care) → payoff (December 2024: mom retired) → guarantee + CTA. 235s video with full transcript. The founder story IS the sales argument — it sells the product and the people simultaneously.
cta: 100% money-back guarantee + 'try Eskiin' — the guarantee lands only after the full emotional investment.
idea: A mini-VSL disguised as a founder story: vision-board open loop → personal story → problem → failed solutions → reframe → mechanism → product → mission → emotional payoff (retiring mom) → guarantee + CTA — where the founder story IS the sales argument.
sequencing: Hook: vision-board open loop — a 16-year-old's goal to retire mom.
Story + failed solutions: eczema and hair loss; medications, shampoos, nothing worked.
Reframe + mechanism: 'Could it be our water?' — the new belief and what's in tap water.
Product: built around everything hated in the alternatives.
Mission zoom-out: the company they wish existed.
Emotional payoff: December 2024 — mom retired.
Guarantee + CTA — only after full emotional investment.
235s video + full transcript.
formatting: Deep-dive copywriting breakdown: the ad's structure decoded beat-by-beat with the psychology labeled per beat, plus a 235s video and full transcript.
why_it_works: The ad earns attention with story before spending any on product — by the CTA, the viewer has bought the founders, so the product is a formality. The mom payoff closes the loop opened in second one.
what_to_steal: The entire arc as LC's founder-story template: Jay's open loop → the problem (jewelry that betrays you) → failed solutions (cheap replacements, 'gold-plated' lies) → reframe → mechanism (PVD over stainless) → product → mission → emotional payoff. 'The founder story IS the sales argument' is LC's brand-content thesis.
